Almost every part of modern society relies on software to function.
Software engineering is an essential profession for the modern world.
Software is abstract and has no physical form.
Software systems come in many forms.
The term 'software engineering' was first suggested in 1968.
'software engineering' was first introduced at a conference held to talk about the 'software crisis.'
Early coding methods failed for large software.
Before 1970s software systems were often unreliable.
Before 1970s software systems often went over budget.
Before 1970s software systems were often delivered late.
New methods in software engineering were developed in the 1970s and 1980s.
Structured programming was developed during the late 1960s and early 1970s.
Object-oriented design and programming originated in the 1960s and 1970s.
Between 1962 and 1967, Ole-Johan Dahl and Kristen Nygaard created Simula.
Between 1962 and 1967, Simula was created at the Norwegian Computing Center.
Simula 67 introduced classes, objects, and inheritance.
Simula 67 is recognized as the first object-oriented language.
In the 1970s, Alan Kay and his team at Xerox PARC created Smalltalk.
Smalltalk made object-oriented programming popular.
Smalltalk gave the official approach to the term 'object-oriented programming'.
In the 1980s, object-oriented design reached the commercial mainstream.
Bjarne Stroustrup began creating C++ in 1979.
C++ initially called 'C with Classes' in 1979.
C++ was released publicly in 1985.
Structured programming developed in the late 1960s and early 1970s.
Structured programming was a direct answer to the 'software crisis.'
Structured programming fixed the heavy reliance on messy GOTO statements.
In 1966, research showed that all programs require only sequence, selection, and iteration.
In 1968, Edsger Dijkstra strongly criticized unstructured coding.
In 1972, an influential book named 'Structured Programming' was published.
Information hiding was developed in 1972.
Computer scientist David Parnas introduced the concept of 'Information Hiding'
Standard software tools and notations were developed throughout the 1970s and 1980s.
Early software tools began as simple command-line compilers and debuggers.
In 1977, UNIX introduced the 'Make' tool to automate building software.
Unix tools like 'grep' and 'diff' simplified code management.
During the 1970s, developers used flowcharts and Data Flow Diagrams.
Entity-Relationship diagrams appeared in 1976 to map database structures.
In the 1980s, visual design methodologies like Booch and OMT grew popular.
Early notations merged into the Unified Modeling Language (UML) in the mid-1990s.
